newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong confident as handover to China nears.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong confident as handover to China nears.

text.p: Most Hong Kong residents are confident the territory will stay prosperous and stable after it reverts to China on July 1, results of a government poll showed on Monday.
The data, released 85 days before Britain hands Hong Kong back to China, showed 76 percent of the respondents were satisfied with the present situation in the territory.

The figure, up three points from a survey in January, came from a poll conducted by the Home Affairs Branch in March, the government said. The department polled 1,526 respondents, aged between 15 and 64, via telephone.
Some 73 percent, unchanged from January, expressed confidence when asked if they thought Hong Kong would continue to be prosperous and stable.
Twenty-four percent expected the situation to improve in the next 12 months while 49 percent said it would be unchanged, compared with 25 and 45 percent in January.
Some 53 percent were satisfied with the performance of the government, up from 48 percent in the last poll.

However, many complained about bread-and-butter issues. Housing was cited by 66 percent as the top problem in the territory, with social welfare and labour-related headaches tying for second place at 25 percent.
